title: Does co-administration of cannabidiol (CBD) influence the plasma availability of delta-9-tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) and its active metabolite in humans? A systematic review and meta-analysis
title_zh: 共给药大麻二酚（CBD）是否影响人类血浆中四氢大麻酚（THC）及其活性代谢物的可用性？系统综述与荟萃分析
abstract: BACKGROUND: Research on the pharmacokinetic influence of cannabidiol (CBD) on delta-9-tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) has produced equivocal results. METHODS: We conducted a systematic search following PRISMA guidelines (last search: 24th November 2025, PROSPERO: CRD42023480695). Included studies were acute dosing trials that administered a) a single, fixed dose of THC and b) a matched dose of THC co-administered with CBD. Our objective was to investigate between-group differences in the Cmax, AUCt and AUCinf of circulating THC and its active metabolite, 11-hydroxy-THC (11-OH-THC). Hedges' g and ratio of means (RoM) were pooled from random-effects meta-analyses. The dose-effects of CBD and THC on Hedges' g were explored using meta-regression. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Collaboration tool RoB 2. RESULTS: 14 studies were included (12 crossover, two parallel group; seven oral administration, five inhalation, one IV, one mixed IV and oral; total participants: 341). In meta-analyses, average AUCt of THC was significantly higher in CBD co-administration study arms versus THC-only (Hedges' g= 0.526, 95%CI= 0.222-0.830), with very low certainty evidence. Both Cmax and AUCt of 11-OH-THC were significantly higher in CBD co-administration study arms (Cmax: g= 0.428, 0.115-0.741; AUCt: g= 0.692, 0.284-1.099), both with medium certainty evidence. In meta-regression analyses, CBD demonstrated dose effects on the Hedges' g of the Cmax and AUCt of 11-OH-THC (P < 0.05), but not THC levels. CONCLUSIONS: Cannabis users and prescribers of cannabinoid-based products should be made aware of the potential for drug-drug pharmacokinetic interactions between CBD and THC.
abstract_zh: 背景：关于大麻二酚（CBD）对四氢大麻酚（THC）药代动力学影响的研究结果不一。方法：我们按照PRISMA指南进行系统检索（最新检索：2025年11月24日，PROSPERO：CRD42023480695）。纳入研究为急性剂量试验，分别给药 a）单一固定剂量的THC 和 b）与CBD共给的匹配剂量THC。我们的目标是研究两组之间循环THC及其活性代谢物11-羟基-THC（11-OH-THC）的Cmax、AUCt和AUCinf差异。采用Hedges’ g和均值比（RoM）进行随机效应荟萃分析。使用元回归探讨CBD和THC剂量对Hedges’ g的影响。使用Cochrane合作工具RoB 2评估偏倚风险。结果：共纳入14项研究（12项交叉设计，2项平行组；7项口服，5项吸入，1项静脉注射，1项混合静脉注射和口服；总参与者341人）。荟萃分析显示，CBD共给组的THC平均AUCt显著高于仅给THC组（Hedges’ g=0.526，95%CI=0.222-0.830），证据质量极低。11-OH-THC的Cmax和AUCt在CBD共给组也显著更高（Cmax：g=0.428，0.115-0.741；AUCt：g=0.692，0.284-1.099），证据质量中等。元回归分析显示，CBD对11-OH-THC的Cmax和AUCt的Hedges’ g具有剂量效应（P<0.05），但对THC水平无显著影响。结论：大麻使用者和处方者应了解CBD与THC之间潜在的药物-药物药代动力学相互作用。
